newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast "racks" keep CARB diesel weak Tues.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast "racks" keep CARB diesel weak Tues.

text.p: Spot prices for U.S. West Coast CARB diesel fell Tuesday, amid lower "rack" prices and new inventory data which showed growing stocks, traders said.
CARB diesel in Los Angeles fell two cents to 65/66 cents a gallon Tuesday, a drop of six cents, or eight percent, from a week ago, traders said.
Plentiful distillate stocks, which stood 1.1 million barrels over last year, prompted refiners like Atlantic Richfield Co. to drop diesel prices at distrbution terminals, or "racks," traders said.
Racks have fallen five cents to 68 cents the last week.
That prompted wholesale prices, which feed terminals, to fall as well.
"ARCO's really driving it down," a trader claimed.
Trucks pick up diesel and other light products at terminals, or "racks," which are generally about two cents more expensive than wholesale prices at the refinery.
Meanwhile, unleaded gasoline for sale in California (CARB) was unchanged on the day at 68/69 cents a gallon, caught between a rally in energy futures and pressure from rising stocks.
Buyers fled the market early, as unleaded futures prices, a catalyst for West Coast price swings, jumped 1.02 cents a gallon Tuesday to 63.36 cents.
"Sellers were moving numbers up and buyers were not chasing them....they were paralyzed by the Merc (New York Mercantile Exchange)," a trader said.
But in the after-hours ACCESS market, prices were hit by weakness, after the American Petroleum Institute (API) a 1.4 million-barrel rise last week in West Coast gasoline stocks.
Conventional gasoline and other distillates stayed flat Tueday, traders said.
